PullRequest.Title: Agent files: VS Code-only options under a vscode: key
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #348915

An agent file can declare VS Code-only options under one `vscode:` key, so it stays a standard agent file that other harnesses read, skipping one unknown key:

```yaml
vscode:
  empty-chat-message:
    markdown: Hi! What went wrong in this window? Describe it below, or start with a screenshot.
    buttons:                      # the first one is the primary button
      - label: Attach a screenshot
        icon: device-camera
        command: workbench.action.chat.attachAppWindowScreenshot
        args: [...]               # optional; without them the command gets { sessionResource }
  assisted-approval-instructions: |
    ...
```

- **`empty-chat-message`:** rendered like an agent response in the empty chat, instead of the welcome. It disappears with the first request and is not part of the transcript. Buttons run any command (agent files are trusted). Unquoted YAML scalars in `args` keep their types. The message and its buttons are readable in the chat accessible view while the chat is empty. A component fixture (`chatCommandButton`) shows the buttons.
- **`assisted-approval-instructions`:** the agent host appends them to the user's own Assisted permissions instructions while the agent is selected, and reapplies them after create, resume and agent changes. Agents forwarded from VS Code reach the runtime under a generated name without a path, so the host finds the agent file through the session's customization snapshot.

**Example:** Team Tools' Agent Fix agent (microsoft/vscode-packages#453), whose agent file uses the options above, in a new chat window. The message and the screenshot button come from `empty-chat-message`; "Explain the bug" is its `argument-hint` (#349049). Code OSS built from this PR combined with #349048 and #349049:

![Agent Fix agent in an empty chat window](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3cd150f-e5b9-46b7-b94b-4819c0f2fc42)

Split from #348918.

**Validation:** core typecheck; PromptValidator and CopilotSessionLauncher unit tests. Tested manually in Code OSS with Team Tools' Agent Fix agent: the empty chat shows its message and screenshot button, and a logpoint in the agent host showed the judge receiving the agent's instructions.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The send and /fleet paths await _prepareSdkTurn, which always awaits this synchronization. The new discovery call precedes the existing equality check. Resume initializes _lastAppliedAgent to undefined, and the helper never stores its getCurrent result. These are direct static call-path facts; actual RPC and file-read durations are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Stdio runtime RPC round trips, agent-file reads and buffers, and YAML parsing work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One additional agent.getCurrent RPC per synchronization for a resumed wrapper until an explicit selection establishes _lastAppliedAgent; one file read/parse per synchronization when its selected agent resolves to a file. Synchronization occurs at initialization, each turn, agent changes, and root-config changes; root-config work scales with live sessions, not all discovered agents.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional serial latency before model requests and repeated filesystem/CPU work, including on warm turns with unchanged or absent guidance.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With unchanged user instructions, synchronization compared the configured string to _appliedAssistedApprovalInstructions and returned without agent-discovery RPCs or agent-file reads.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every synchronization now discovers agent guidance before checking whether the applied instructions changed. Resumed sessions repeatedly query the current agent, and sessions with a resolvable custom-agent file repeatedly read and parse it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 9539 awaits _readAgentAssistedApprovalInstructions before the unchanged-value return. Added lines 9568-9573 query agent.getCurrent when _lastAppliedAgent is undefined and call parseAgentFile without retaining either discovery result.
Findings.Title: Keep unchanged turns on the no-I/O guidance path
Findings.Impact: Continuing a resumed conversation now waits for an extra runtime round trip before every request, even with the default agent. Custom-agent conversations additionally reload their agent file on each turn, delaying dispatch unnecessarily; unrelated root-config updates repeat discovery across live sessions.
Findings.Evidence: _prepareSdkTurn at 7627-7635 runs this synchronization for normal session.send (7389-7403) and /fleet (7665). _initializeSdkWrapper sets _lastAppliedAgent to undefined for resumes at 5168. The new helper leaves that field unchanged, so successful getCurrent calls repeat even when no custom agent exists. parseAgentFile at pluginParsers.ts:1294-1296 reads the entire file and parses YAML on every invocation. CopilotAgent constructs the runtime connection with RuntimeConnection.forStdio at copilotAgent.ts:5273. Root-config changes also invoke synchronization for every subscribed live session at 9414-9416.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve and retain the restored selection, including no selection, per SDK wrapper. Cache selected-agent guidance including absence, invalidate it on agent/file/customization changes, and reset wrapper-specific state on relaunch so unchanged turns retain the existing no-I/O fast path.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Widget attachment, mode changes, and view-model changes invoke _update without checking transcript contents or visibility. The consumer explicitly mounts the result only when there are zero items. File reads and markdown/code-tokenization work are established by their implementations; greeting sizes and observed UI delays are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Unnecessary agent-file reads and remote filesystem calls, markdown parsing/sanitization, code-block tokenization, and allocated greeting DOM/listeners.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One fresh file read per custom-agent widget update when its file has no open text model, plus one full greeting render when the header defines a message. Work scales with restored widgets and conversation/mode switches, and rendering with greeting size; there is no per-URI coalescing across widgets.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Avoidable remote/local I/O and renderer CPU/allocation during existing-conversation restoration and switching, with hidden greeting resources retained per widget.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening or switching an existing conversation performed no agent-file reads or rendering for this empty-chat greeting.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new contribution reads every selected custom agent's file on each update and constructs its greeting whenever present, even when the widget already contains a transcript and cannot display it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 82-85 invoke _update on mode/view-model changes and attachment. Added line 92 unconditionally reads a non-builtin mode's URI, and added line 101 renders its message without an empty-transcript check.
Findings.Title: Skip greeting reads and rendering for populated chats
Findings.Impact: Restoring or switching among existing custom-agent conversations performs greeting work that can never be visible. Remote agent files add stat/read traffic even when they have no greeting, while greetings with formatted examples additionally trigger markdown rendering and syntax tokenization on the UI thread.
Findings.Evidence: _read uses IPromptsService.parseNew at line 108. promptsServiceImpl.ts:839-849 reuses an open text model, but otherwise calls fileService.readFile and parses afresh; it has no closed-file cache. _render at 125-126 invokes the markdown renderer, which synchronously parses/sanitizes markdown (base/browser/markdownRenderer.ts:224-262) and invokes the default code-block renderer. EditorMarkdownCodeBlockRenderer.renderCodeBlock tokenizes fenced examples at line 50. Meanwhile chatWidget.ts:1739-1746 mounts this content only when numItems is zero. For vscode-remote agent files, RemoteFileSystemProviderClient uses DiskFileSystemProviderClient, whose stat/readFile methods cross the remote channel.
Findings.Recommendation: Check that the transcript is empty before loading the greeting and again after the asynchronous read before rendering it. Refresh when the widget becomes empty, and release the greeting when leaving that state; defer hidden-widget rendering until it can be shown.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show a custom agent's greeting in a new empty chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget attachment or mode/view-model changes asynchronously load the selected file. Workbench restoration and input do not await _update, but displaying the greeting requires parsing the file and constructing its DOM. Markdown parsing/sanitization runs on the renderer thread after the read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected agent file and parse its frontmatter and body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical read per update of a custom-agent widget unless that file has an open text model. The file service performs metadata validation and content reading; reads are not grouped across widgets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No greeting-specific agent-file read on widget attachment or mode/view-model changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before this greeting can appear, but not awaited by overall workbench restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For vscode-remote agent files without an open text model, issue remote metadata and content requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A stat request and a readFile request per logical read with the inspected provider capabilities; the file service starts validation and reading in parallel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No remote filesystem requests attributable to greeting loading.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The greeting waits for the remote read and validation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load image resources referenced by greeting markdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the distinct uncached image URLs in each constructed greeting; browser HTTP caching and in-flight coalescing can reduce network requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The custom greeting and its image elements did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Image display is asynchronous; text and input need not wait for image completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of attached custom-agent widgets and update events; agent-file bytes, greeting markdown length, fenced code blocks, buttons, and image URLs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are fire-and-forget with no global limiter or per-widget sequencing. Multiple reads may overlap; post-read widget/mode checks reject obsolete modes. Code-block renderers run asynchronously, with grammar creation potentially cached but text tokenization repeated.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: parseNew reuses an open model's parsed representation but otherwise rereads/reparses files. The contribution has no URI cache or pending-read coalescing, including for files with no greeting. Rendered stores are replaced per update and disposed when the widget is removed. Browser image caching remains applicable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: attachment/event subscriptions, parseNew's implementation, and renderer calls were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Greeting size and event overlap are unmeasured. A short text greeting is inexpensive; code examples and remote files increase cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Initial work for a visible empty chat implements the feature and is not independently a regression. Unconditional execution for populated/hidden chats is covered by the eager-work finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore or switch existing custom-agent conversations, including hidden registered widgets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidChangeViewModel and mode changes launch _update without awaiting it. Existing transcript loading can proceed, but read completions perform markdown rendering and DOM allocation on the same renderer thread. ChatWidget mounts the greeting only when its item count is zero.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload the selected custom agent file despite the existing transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical read per custom-agent update without an open agent-file text model; zero for builtin modes. Each logical read includes metadata and content operations. No grouping across widgets or negative-result caching.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing conversations performed no empty-greeting reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the transcript-loading promise chain, but causes avoidable I/O and schedules renderer CPU work during conversation switching.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remote stat/read requests for workspace agent files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two remote channel requests per logical read for this provider, with stat and content reads overlapping; open text models avoid them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero remote requests for this unused greeting.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by conversation switching itself; completed reads trigger unnecessary parsing/rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and sanitize markdown, create hidden DOM/buttons, and tokenize fenced examples.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One complete greeting render per successful update defining a message, even for an unchanged agent; one tokenization per code block.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No greeting rendering, tokenization, or retained greeting card for this scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Competes with transcript rendering and input on the renderer thread, although the greeting cannot be displayed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing custom-agent conversation/widget count, conversation switches, mode/view-model event count, and greeting/file size—not the number of all discovered agents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All attached widgets can start reads concurrently. Several same-widget updates can overlap and reconstruct the same greeting. Rendering itself executes on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Open models avoid disk reads, but no contribution-level cache/coalescing exists. Absence of a greeting is not memoized. Prior message stores are disposed on replacement/removal, so retention is bounded to one current card per widget rather than an unbounded historical leak.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _update lacks any empty/visible guard, while the sole widget mounting branch explicitly requires zero transcript items.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote latency, greeting complexity, and number of restored widgets vary; no runtime timing measurements were available.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: skip reads and rendering when the empty-chat feature cannot be displayed, with state rechecked after asynchronous reads.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initialize/resume an SDK session or explicitly change its selected agent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: _initializeSdkWrapper awaits guidance synchronization before readiness. setAgent awaits agent selection/deselection and then the newly added synchronization before the owning chat operation finishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the runtime's restored current agent over the SDK's stdio runtime connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query when _lastAppliedAgent is undefined, including during resumed-wrapper initialization. Created sessions already know their selected agent or null.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initialization applied user instructions without querying the current agent for guidance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before resumed session initialization can complete.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse one resolved selected-agent file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one agent-file read per synchronization, not one per discovered agent. Name resolution scans the customization catalog in memory; known null selection skips the read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No agent-file read in instruction synchronization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before readiness or explicit agent-switch completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply combined user and selected-agent approval instructions to the runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configure call only if the combined text differs from the applied text. Initial application remains existing behavior; applying after agent switches is a new placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initialization configured user instructions when changed; setAgent did not synchronize agent-specific instructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before readiness or agent-switch completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session creates/resumes/relaunches and explicit agent switches; one selected file per synchronization plus an in-memory scan of custom-agent metadata.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Guidance synchronization is serialized per session with Sequencer. Agent operations are serialized by the owning chat queue. Independent sessions can initialize concurrently; the added lookup does not spawn another runtime.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _lastAppliedAgent is known for creates and explicit switches, but remains undefined after a resumed-agent lookup. _appliedAssistedApprovalInstructions deduplicates configure calls only, after file discovery. File contents and absence of guidance are not cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initialization, setAgent, helper, file-service implementation, and RuntimeConnection.forStdio configuration were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Initial file/RPC duration and custom-agent prevalence are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: Discovering and applying guidance once at these lifecycle boundaries is justified. Repeating the same discovery on subsequent unchanged turns/config notifications is the separately reported regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send follow-up requests or start /fleet with unchanged agent guidance
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Normal send and /fleet await _prepareSdkTurn, which awaits _syncAssistedApprovalInstructions before SDK request dispatch. Newly inserted discovery occurs before the existing unchanged-text fast path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query rpc.agent.getCurrent across the existing stdio runtime connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional RPC per synchronization for a resumed wrapper until an explicit selection sets _lastAppliedAgent. This includes default-agent sessions; the successfully resolved absence is not retained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged instruction text caused no guidance-discovery RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a serial runtime round trip before each request. The control-plane timeout is 30 seconds; actual successful-call latency is unknown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse the selected agent file, even when it contains no assisted approval instructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical file read/parse per synchronization when the selected agent resolves to a URI. The file service validates metadata and reads content; there is no guidance cache or conditional etag read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Warm unchanged turns compared cached/configured instruction strings without reading an agent file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request cannot be dispatched until the read/parse completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update runtime instructions if their combined text actually changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero calls on unchanged text, even after the unnecessary discovery; at most one if text differs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same configure-call deduplication for unchanged user instructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only an actual update awaits this pre-existing configure boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of turns and guidance synchronizations per SDK wrapper; selected agent-file size. Counts are per session/turn, not per item in its agent catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is serialized by the per-session guidance sequencer and awaited in the serial turn-preparation chain. Different chat sessions may proceed concurrently; configure deduplication does not coalesce the preceding reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The applied-text cache does not avoid preceding discovery. Resumed selection remains unknown in host state after successful lookup; custom-file contents and negative guidance results are never memoized. OS caching can reduce physical disk latency but not logical reads, allocations, or parsing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call sites establish dispatch gating and repeated successful work independently of timing estimates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime load, filesystem latency, and file sizes affect delay. No benchmark or measured latency is asserted.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: retain resolved agent identity and cache guidance with lifecycle/file-change invalidation so unchanged turns do not repeat I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Propagate root-configuration changes across live SDK sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each live session's root-config subscription schedules guidance synchronization. This is background work for the settings update, but later turn preparation joins that session's guidance sequencer and can wait behind it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query current agents for resumed sessions whose selection is still undefined.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per queued synchronization per such live session, even when the changed root setting does not affect approval instructions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged instruction strings returned without agent queries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initially background; can delay later turns through the per-session sequencer and compete on the runtime connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reload the selected agent file for each live session with a resolvable custom selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical read per queued synchronization per applicable live session; sessions sharing an agent URI do not share the result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unrelated config changes required only inexpensive instruction comparison for this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background I/O and parsing can accumulate ahead of a subsequent turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live applicable sessions multiplied by root-config notifications, not the number of agents per session. Each session reads at most its selected file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized within each session; no global discovery limiter. Independent session sequencers can perform reads/RPCs concurrently, while repeated notifications queue within each session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The applied-text cache avoids redundant configure RPCs but not discovery. No positive/negative guidance cache and no cross-session URI coalescing are present.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: unfiltered root-config subscription and new pre-deduplication discovery are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical live-session counts and root-config notification frequency are unknown; this is an amplifier of the reported repeated-work issue, not a separately measured burst.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the host guidance finding; not reported separately because it shares the same pre-deduplication discovery mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover, parse, and validate agent files containing the vscode header
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing discovery reads and parses each candidate file before exposing agent metadata. Validation adds vscode to an existing supported-attribute list; it does not schedule another scan or file read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read discovered agent files and parse their metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one parseAgentFile call per discovered component before name deduplication. The diff adds nested-map lookups and an optional extracted string, not additional discovery reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery file reads and YAML parse already occurred; assisted guidance was not extracted.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Existing discovered agent-file count and header size. Changed work is a pair of property searches and optional string trimming per parsed file.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: readAgentComponents retains its existing Promise.all behavior; workbench discovery retains its existing queueDiscoveryRead limiter. No additional per-agent boundary fan-out is introduced inside discovery.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No discovery cache or invalidation policy is changed. Existing workbench model-backed parse reuse and discovery scheduling remain in place. The new host/UI reads described above are separate callers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete parser/validator hunks and surrounding discovery call sites were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Additional property-lookup/string costs are unmeasured but bounded by each already-parsed header.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent reportable regression in metadata extraction, supported-attribute validation, tests, CSS, or the component fixture. No concrete performance-regression fix requiring provenance collection was identified.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read a greeting in the accessible view or activate its command button
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the accessible view uses the already-computed plaintext and actions. Button activation calls the selected command once; only that requested action waits for its existing service operations. No command runs merely because a greeting is rendered.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For the documented screenshot command, check screen permission where needed, enumerate windows, and capture the chosen window through nativeHostService; existing fallback uses browser media capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command invocation per button activation. Normal capture lists windows once, may repeat interactively when platform selection requires it, and attempts one native capture with a media fallback. It does not capture once per window in the list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command and capture workflow were available from existing commands/keybindings/context actions; the diff adds a button entry point without amplifying an individual command's work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Screenshot attachment waits for capture; greeting rendering and accessible-view opening do not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit button activations and captured image size. Accessible-view setup copies the button action array once per opening; it does not reread files or rerender the greeting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each click invokes one existing command; the diff adds no automatic retries or per-window capture loop. Button and markdown listeners are owned by the per-widget DisposableStore, removed on replacement/widget removal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Accessible text is generated when the card is rendered and reused by the accessible provider. Actions reference the current session at invocation. Native capture caching/lifecycle is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for single-invocation behavior and the documented screenshot path; arbitrary user-declared commands necessarily have their own unrelated implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Capture duration and arbitrary command costs vary, but no changed multiplicity was found in the invocation path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No independent performance regression. Existing capture boundaries are intentionally reachable from the new user action; no speculative findings for arbitrary commands or correctness-only accessibility behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 15 changed files and all diff pages against base 36e8c0289a5f29eae15a933263220d9895302ff6. Submitted two high-confidence findings: guidance discovery now repeats ahead of the warm per-turn fast path, and greeting work is performed for populated/hidden chats. Accounted for initialization, selection, root-config fan-out, discovery, rendering, accessibility, and command activation with effective cache/concurrency/cardinality analysis. Read-only static review; no concrete removed performance mechanism qualified for regression-fix provenance reporting.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
